item.title: Jack Bech prepares for emotional game in New Orleans, where his brother was killed
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When the Raiders face the Saints on Sunday in the Superdome, the game will have significant meaning for Las Vegas receiver Jack Bech.
item.content:encoded:
When the Raiders face the Saints on Sunday in the Superdome, the game will have significant meaning for Las Vegas receiver Jack Bech.

Bech's brother, Tiger, was killed in a New Orleans terrorist attack on New Year's Day in 2025, along with 13 others.

“I just want to rewrite this wrong in New Orleans,” Bech told Sam Warren of The Athletic earlier this week. “Get that nasty, dirty taste out of our mouth.”

It will be Jack Bech's first NFL game in New Orleans, the city to which his family would travel to watch Saints games when he and Tiger were growing up.

Jack Bech has been fueled by his brother's memory. And their childhood memories include attending games at the Superdome and dreaming of playing there one day.

Bech said that it "would mean everything" to Tiger to see Jack achieve that dream.

“I know he couldn’t be any happier right now,” Bech said.

A second-round pick of the Raiders in 2025, Bech has caught five passes for 48 yards and a touchdown in two 2026 games. As the Raiders try to move to a surprising 3-0 record (after going 3-14 last year), Jack Bech will be ready to make an impact.

The challenge will be to control and direct the emotions he'll be feeling. Receiver coach Zach Azzani has been helping Bech find the right balance.

“He said, ‘Play the game with emotions; don’t be emotional,’” Bech told Warren. “It’s something that’s been super helpful for me. . . Give it everything, leave everything on that field and see what happens by the end of the game."

Whatever happens, Jack Bech will surely be feeling the presence of his brother in a building where they enjoyed watching Saints games as boys.

item.title: Through two weeks, several seats are heating up
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: 10 of 32 jobs opened after 2025. Surely, more will be vacant in January.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL means plenty of things, from No Fun League to Not For Long. That's never been more true for coaches.

Last year, 10 of 32 jobs became open. Whatever the number this time around, the number will be closer to nine than none.

Through two weeks, more than a few seats are getting hot. Or, as the case may be, hotter.

We'll start with Colts coach Shane Steichen, mainly because of what team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said after the 2025 season ended: "We have been very clear with [G.M.] Chris [Ballard] and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher."

So far, the Colts are winless. The defense has given up more than 500 yards in each of the first two games. Obviously, something needs to change or there will be a housecleaning in Indianapolis.

Next on the list is Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles. Since starting 2025 with a 6-2 record, the Buccaneers are 2-11. Imagine the angst in the Glazer suite last week while they had to sit there and wait two hours for the likely loss to the lowly Browns to become official. A turnaround is a must.

Jets coach Aaron Glenn wasn't one-and-done after 2025, in part due to a buyout that would have exceeded $40 million. The season started with a suffocation of the Titans and former Jets coach Robert Saleh. In Week 2, a blown 10-point lead, widely-criticized late-game clock management, and a decision to receive the opening kickoff of overtime have increased the pressure on Glenn to do more this year than he did last year.

Things are looking grim for Dan Quinn in D.C. For some, it's already become a given that Quinn will be gone after his third season — especially if it's another 5-12 showing, or worse. The latest Jayden Daniels dislocated left elbow likely won't buy Quinn a mulligan.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur is facing an uprising in the land of beef and cheese. Yes, he got an extension after the 2025 season. But he wouldn't be the first coach who received a new contract one offseason and a pink slip the next.

Lastly, we'll mention Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh. He made the playoffs in each of his first two years on the job. This year, however, has started in disastrous fashion. He has two years left on his five-year, $80 million contract after 2026; the buyout could buy him one more year. It all comes down to whether the Chargers play dramatically better than they did against two teams that combined in 2025 for a record of 6-28.

Any, some, or all of the coaches listed above could turn things around. After all, 15 games remain. And other coaches who are currently safe could end up in hot water as the season unfolds.

Either way, it makes sense to be watching the situation closely, because the NFL head-coaching industry has proven to be a high-turnover business. And, as former Cardinals coach Jonathan Gannon acknowledged once it became clear he was on the hot seat in 2025, it's the business they've chosen.

item.content:encoded:
A pair of Panthers wide receivers carry questionable tags into Sunday's game in Cleveland and it looks like at least one of them will be able to play.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Jalen Coker is expected to play. Coker has been dealing with an ankle injury for the last couple of weeks and was limited in practice on Friday.

Xavier Legette was also limited on Friday after missing Thursday's practice with a knee injury that popped up during the week. He is viewed as a game-time decision for the 1-1 Panthers.

The wideouts are the only questionable players for Carolina. Linebacker Devin Lloyd and safety Nick Scott have been ruled out.

item.title: Justin Fields could be returning to New York
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Woody Johnson's favorite quarterback could be returning to New York.
item.content:encoded:
Woody Johnson's favorite quarterback could be returning to New York.

Justin Fields, who was traded by the Jets to the Chiefs as part of the plan to have a capable replacement in the event Patrick Mahomes wasn't ready for Week 1, has emerged as an option for the Giants, who have made it clear they will look at all options.

Fields has been mentioned multiple times in recent days by multiple reporters, which means that the word is out that Fields could be a possibility for the Giants.

The Giants are expected to make a move as soon as Monday. Jameis Winston's performance against the Titans on Sunday will surely be a factor in the question of whether they're looking for someone to serve as Winston's backup — or someone who could eventually supplant him while starter Jaxson Dart misses at least the balance of the regular season after knee surgery.

The two-year, $40 million contract Fields signed last year with the Jets included $10 million guaranteed for 2026. The Chiefs are paying him $3 million, and the Jets are paying $7 million. With Mahomes looking like Mahomes again, the Chiefs could recoup their 2027 sixth-round pick and unload the balance of Fields's 2026 salary.

The Chiefs also would have to be willing to elevate rookie Garrett Nussmeier into the QB2 role behind Mahomes, unless coach Andy Reid and G.M. Brett Veach have someone else in mind who could be the backup to Mahomes.

Giants coach John Harbaugh has limited experience against Fields. In 2021, Fields (then a rookie with the Bears), started a Week 11 game against the Ravens. He left with a rib injury after completing four of 11 passes for 79 yards and rushing one time for four yards. During his single season with the Steelers, Fields played three snaps in a Week 11 game against the Ravens that Russell Wilson started. Fields ran the ball twice for 17 yards. In the wild-card game that same year between the Steelers and Ravens, Fields played two snaps, throwing one pass that did not connect.

Still, Fields apparently is on the radar screen for a return to New York, where the other team that plays in MetLife Stadium will be paying him a lot more than whatever the Giants would contribute to his 2026 W-2.

item.title: Mike Evans is expected to play on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The 49ers will try to improve to 3-0 on the season when they host the Cardinals on Sunday and it looks like wide receiver Mike Evans will be part of that effort.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers will try to improve to 3-0 on the season when they host the Cardinals on Sunday and it looks like wide receiver Mike Evans will be part of that effort.

Evans was listed as questionable on Friday due to a hip injury that caused him to miss two days of practice. He returned for a limited workout on Friday and Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that he plans to be in the lineup on Sunday afternoon.

Evans has nine catches for 103 yards and a touchdown so far this season.

The 49ers have dealt with a number of injuries at wide receiver since the start of training camp and they placed Demarcus Robinson on injured reserve Saturday. De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, and Christian Kirk were already on that list, which leaves Deebo Samuel, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, and KhaDarel Hodge to go with Evans against Arizona.

item.title: Report: Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Expected 3-4 week absence is on the low end for a Grade 2 strain.
item.content:encoded:
As of last Sunday night, there was optimism that an MRI would show that Bears quarterback Caleb Williams had suffered a Grade 1 hamstring injury. For six days, the Bears managed to keep the specific degree of the strain secret.

The secret is now out. ESPN reports that it’s a Grade 2 injury, which "could" keep Williams out of action for three to four weeks.

That's on the short end of the usual window for a Grade 2 hamstring strain — three to eight weeks.

Whatever the specific grade (and there are surely shades of gray between 1 and 2), a hamstring injury needs time to recover. And then even more time. It can feel fine with normal running. Then, when the athlete hits full speed in a game, it can grab. And then it's aggravated. And more time can be missed.

Tyson Bagent, once cleared from a concussion he suffered last Sunday, will be the starter. Case Keenum is Bagent's backup.

Williams has already been ruled out for Monday night's game against the Eagles. In Week 4, the Bears host the Jets before traveling to Green Bay and then Atlanta. Next up will be the two Super Bowl teams, with a home game against the Patriots in Week 7 and a Monday night visit to Seattle in Week 8.

item.title: Desman Stephens II returned to sideline after hit that sent Dante Moore to the hospital
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Saturday night's game between Oregon and USC included a hit from Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II that knocked out Ducks quarterback Dante Moore and sent him to the hospital.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday night's game between Oregon and USC included a hit from Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II that knocked out Ducks quarterback Dante Moore and sent him to the hospital. Beyond the play itself, the situation was riddled with horrible optics.

Stephens celebrated after the play. He was seen smiling on the sideline before his disqualification.

Then, in the second half, Stephens returned to the USC sideline.

Asked after the game why Stephens was back on the sideline, USC coach Lincoln Riley seemed to be confused by the question. "Because he’s on our football team," Riley said.

Strangely, NCAA rules allow a "disqualified" player to remain on the sidelines. (An "ejected" player must leave.) It was nevertheless tone deaf for USC to allow him to return.

Stephens deserves a stiff suspension both for the hit and for his antics after it. And there's no way USC will do that on its own. The NCAA needs to step in and send a clear message about its commitment to player health and safety. If it doesn't, someone should suggest an amendment to the "Protect College Sports Act" that mandates the NCAA to take a harder line when something like this happens.

While the name of the bill is simply a slogan aimed at getting the NCAA the antitrust exemption it craves, the NCAA coined the term in order to make the bill seem more palatable. So they're now stuck with it. And, given the chosen title of the bill, how can the NCAA and the federal government "protect college sports" if they don't also protect college athletes?

item.title: Report: "Handful" of teams have begun inquiring about Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Cowboys and Lions reportedly have called.
item.content:encoded:
Asked this week if he'll be playing at some point, Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. told reporters, "Yeah, definitely."

He wasn't asked to specify whether that would be with the Steelers or a new team.

As Porter's contract impasse with the Steelers extends to a third week — and, potentially, a third missed game on Sunday due to "conditioning" — more teams reportedly are reaching out to Pittsburgh about a possible trade.

Last week, the official word from ESPN was that the Steelers had received no "serious inquiries" about Porter. PFT thereafter reported that at least one team has called.

Now, ESPN reports that a "handful" of teams "have begun making inquiries" about a possible trade for Porter. The Steelers reportedly "would be willing to listen," but they would want a "strong compensation package."

That's where a wacky situation gets even more out of whack. If the Steelers want a lot for Porter (we've heard it could be as much as a first-round pick or a second-round pick, plus a third-round pick), why won't they just pay him something closer to what he's seeking? For the interested teams, the challenge becomes giving the Steelers what they want for Porter while also figuring out a new deal with Porter.

The new report identifies the Lions and Cowboys as teams that have called the Steelers.

Dallas would be an interesting destination, given that Porter is represented by the same agent (David Mulugheta) who represents former Cowboys linebacker Micah Parsons. After an ugly contract negotiation, during which Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones disrespected Mulugheta by pretending not to know who he is, the Cowboys traded Parsons to the Packers once it became clear that Parsons would not play without a new contract.

The trade deadline arrives in 44 days, on the Tuesday after Week 9. The sooner a trade happens, the faster the Steelers and Porter extricate themselves from a situation that gets more awkward by the day. Porter clearly isn't playing because he doesn't have a new contract, and the Steelers have painted themselves into a corner with their outdated internal rule that new contracts won't be done after the regular season starts.

item.title: Justin Herbert could pass to his brother as Chargers elevate tight end Patrick Herbert
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The younger Herbert brother will be active for the Chargers for the first time today.
item.content:encoded:
The Herbert brothers could have a special moment today in Buffalo.

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert's little brother, tight end Patrick Herbert, has been elevated from the Chargers' practice squad to the active roster. That means the Herberts are set to play together today against the Bills.

When the Chargers added Patrick to their practice squad just before the start of this season, it made the Herberts teammates for the first time since they were at Oregon in 2019. Patrick barely played as a true freshman that year, and Justin never threw him a pass.

The 25-year-old Patrick, who is three years younger than Justin, signed with the Jaguars as an undrafted free agent last year and spent the season on their practice squad. He remained with the Jaguars throughout this offseason.

Patrick spent six seasons at Oregon, playing there from 2019 through 2024. As a freshman he got on the field for two games, while Justin was leading the Ducks to a 12-2 record that culminated in winning the Rose Bowl. During his college career, Patrick caught 31 passes for 388 yards and four touchdowns.

If Justin throws a touchdown pass to Patrick, he'd do something the NFL hasn't seen in almost a century. Via Sal Paolantonio of ESPN, the last time an NFL player threw a touchdown pass to his brother, it was Red Grange to Gardie Grange for the Chicago Bears against the Minneapolis Red Jackets on October 27, 1929. The only other brother-to-brother touchdown pass was Cobb Rooney to Bill Rooney for the Duluth Kelleys against the Kenosha Maroons on October 26, 1924.

item.title: Report: Myles Garrett will need about six weeks to recover from knee surgery
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Garrett might not be back until Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.content:encoded:
The season may be about half over when Rams defensive end Myles Garrett next takes the field.

Garrett will need about six weeks to recover from knee surgery, according to Ian Rapoport.

After struggling to play through his knee injury in the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers, Garrett had knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve. By rule, players on injured reserve have to miss at least four weeks, but it appears that Garrett will be out longer than that.

The Rams' Week 9 game against the Commanders on November 8 now looks like his most likely return date, although Garrett is reportedly hoping to return sooner.

Garrett didn't practice much in training camp or play at all in the preseason as he dealt with what the team was calling knee swelling. The injury proved to be more significant than thought when Garrett struggled through the Week 1 loss.

The Rams traded for Garrett because they thought he could put them over the top in their quest to win the Super Bowl. He may still do that, but it's going to be a while before he does anything to help the Rams win.

item.title: Oregon coach Dan Lanning blasts "disgusting play" by USC that injured Dante Moore
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Oregon coach Dan Lanning was furious after Saturday's win over USC at the illegal play that knocked Ducks quarterback Dante Moore out of the game and sent him to the hospital.
item.content:encoded:
Oregon coach Dan Lanning was furious after Saturday's win over USC at the illegal play that knocked Ducks quarterback Dante Moore out of the game and sent him to the hospital.

Moore, a potential first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, was sliding after running for a first down when he was blasted in the head by USC linebacker Desman Stephens. Lanning did not appreciate it.

"Our guys respect the game. I don't think you'd ever see that from our players. I don't think you'd ever see that from our coaches," Lanning said. "It's a disgusting play. You don't want to see it happen. It's disappointing that it happened. I'm praying that our player's healthy, and I'm praying that their player can learn from that situation."

Lanning credited his team for the way it responded to losing its star quarterback.

"In that moment, everybody wants to go get into a street fight, and I thought our players had unbelievable composure in that moment," Lanning said. "And then they went and played it on the field, which is where the game is meant to be played."

Lanning indicated that Moore's prognosis looks good, but said he wasn't ready to release an update on Moore's condition.

"Indications are that he's in recovery, so I don't want to speak too soon, but he's moving," Lanning said. "He has the ability to move, so we'll continue to assess him, but I don't want to make any speculation on further thoughts on that before we have further information on him."

After Moore was taken to a nearby hospital, he was replaced by Nebraska transfer Dylan Raiola, who had a tremendous game. Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards, with two touchdowns and no turnovers or sacks, as Oregon won 41-27.

item.title: Dante Moore knocked out with brutal hit to the head while sliding
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Moore, a potential first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, was put on a stretcher and carted to an ambulance.
item.content:encoded:
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, a potential first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, took a brutal hit to his head while sliding during today's game against USC and appeared to be unconscious on the field.

Moore ran for 10 yards on second-and-9 in the second quarter and then went into a feet-first slide. After Moore's knee hit the ground, USC's Desman Stephens drove his shoulder into Moore's head, slamming the back of Moore's head into the ground. Moore immediately exhibited the fencing response that frequently comes with serious head trauma.

Moore was on the ground for several minutes before he was placed on a stretcher and carted to an ambulance. He was moving his hands and feet.

Stephens was called for targeting and ejected from the game, and a brawl nearly broke out as several Oregon players went after him and players on both teams began to leave the sideline, although the officials and coaches were able to get things calmed down before it got out of hand.

Moore is one of the most talented quarterbacks in college football and was expected to be a first-round pick this year if he had turned pro. Instead, he decided to stay one more year at Oregon, and now the immediate concern is as much about his health as about his football future.

item.title: NFL fines Tyrique Stevenson $22,342 for hit that knocked off Aaron Jones's helmet
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the fourth quarter of Sunday's Vikings-Bears game in Chicago, a wicked hit sent Minnesota running back Aaron Jones's helmet flying.
item.content:encoded:
In the fourth quarter of Sunday's Vikings-Bears game in Chicago, a wicked hit sent Minnesota running back Aaron Jones's helmet flying. Jones remained in the game.

The player who delivered the hit has been fined.

The NFL imposed a $22,342 sanction on Bears defensive back Tyrique Stevenson for impermissible use of the helmet. The rulebook prohibits a player from lowering his head and making forcible contact with his helmet against an opponent.

The infraction was not flagged; it rarely is. Typically, the situation is addressed with the imposition of a fine.

Impermissible use of the helmet is not one of the five violations that will result in an automatic suspension if there are three violations.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers has gone seven straight games without multiple TD passes
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The final years of Aaron Rodgers's career aren't going as well as the rest of it.
item.content:encoded:
The final years of Aaron Rodgers's career aren't going as well as the rest of it.

He currently has gone seven straight games without throwing multiple touchdown passes. Via NBC Sports research, an eighth game would match the longest streak of his career, which also has happened after he won his fourth NFL MVP award.

From 2022 with the Packers through a quick exit with a torn Achilles tendon in 2023 to the first game of 2024, Rodgers went eight straight games without throwing multiple touchdown passes.

For the season, Rodgers has one touchdown pass and one interception, and a passer rating on 72.1.

On the bright side, a win over the Bengals would tie him with former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger for the fifth most in NFL history, with 165.

item.title: A win on Sunday would tie Dak Prescott with Roger Staubach for second on Cowboys' all-time list
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last week, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott set the team's all-time passing touchdown record.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott set the team's all-time passing touchdown record. Another mark is on the table for Sunday in Rio de Janeiro.

Via NBC Sports research, a win by the Cowboys would tie him with Hall of Famer Roger Staubach for the second-most wins in franchise history, at 85. (Troy Aikman holds the record, with 94.)

Prescott also needs one touchdown pass to get to 250 for his career. If he does it tomorrow, he'll be the ninth fastest in NFL history to reach that mark, in 142 games.

The 1-1 Cowboys need a win to avoid their third straight 1-2 start.

item.title: Former Oklahoma teammates Kyler Murray, Baker Mayfield meet again
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray's return from a Week 1 concussion adds a separate wrinkle to the Week 3 game against the Buccaneers.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray's return from a Week 1 concussion adds a separate wrinkle to the Week 3 game against the Buccaneers.

The game means that former Oklahoma teammates Murray and Baker Mayfield will have their fourth NFL meeting. Murray leads, 3-0.

Mayfield won the Heisman Trophy at Oklahoma in 2017. Murray replaced Mayfield in 2018, and then Murray won it.

Their personal rivalry takes a back seat to the bigger picture. The Vikings hope to get to 3-0, and the Buccaneers need to avoid slipping to 0-3.

And there's one interesting wrinkle that plays into the home team's favor. Mayfield has faced a Brian Flores defense twice in his career. In 2019, Mayfield and the Browns beat the Dolphins. In 2023, Mayfield and the Bucs stunned the Vikings in Flores's first game as the team's defensive coordinator. Mayfield had five touchdown passes and one interception in those two games.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be under a lot of pressure in Sunday's Week 3 matchup vs. the Minnesota Vikings, trying to avoid starting 0-3 for the first time since 2014.

item.title: Steve Sarkisian blames "society" for Colin Simmons's bizarre unsportsmanlike conduct foul
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: To cap a week in which the NFL went overboard with fines, Texas defensive end Colin Simmons did something that possibly would have gotten him banned for life by 345 Park Avenue.
item.content:encoded:
To cap a week in which the NFL went overboard with fines, Texas defensive end Colin Simmons did something that possibly would have gotten him banned for life by 345 Park Avenue.

After one of his Longhorn record-tying five sacks against Tennessee, Simmons celebrated by pretending to urinate on the field.

He seemed surprised when the officials penalized the move, with the eventual explanation being that Simmons was "simulating using the restroom."

Coach Steve Sarkisian addressed the situation following the 20-17 win.

“We took him out," Sarkisian said, via Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing, regarding the fact that Simmons, well, took it out. "We addressed it, and put him back in. I’m not gonna give the guy the death penalty over an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. We’ve got to fix it though. That can’t continue as we move forward.”

That part is reasonable and appropriate. Then, things got a little screwy from Sarkisian.

“Unfortunately, in our society right now, we live in the ‘look at me’ society," Sarkisian said. "All of you guys have your Twitter accounts, and as fast as you can type something because you want everyone to look at your account, and you get clicks. Well, that’s the world that we live in. So we’ve got to get to —it’s about the team and focus on the team, and not so much ‘look at me.’ So we’ll try to improve upon that, but five sacks was pretty cool today too.”

Steve, don't simulate using the restroom on our leg and tell us it's raining. Society didn't lead Simmons to do something we've never seen a player do, because 99.999999 percent of all players know not to do it.

Still, we'd love to hear how Sarkisian would explain a similarly perverse celebration that was not penalized. Almost as much as we'd love to hear the explanation of the foul.

item.title: Deion Sanders says Colorado is better than the score shows after another loss
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Colorado lost its second consecutive game today, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he's struggling to figure out why his team's results aren't what they should be.
item.content:encoded:
Colorado lost its second consecutive game today, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he's struggling to figure out why his team's results aren't what they should be.

"We're better than this. It seems as though we're better than our opponents, but the score does not dictate that. And that's the fascinating thing, we've got to find out why," Sanders said after Colorado's 23-13 loss at Baylor.

With Colorado struggling at halftime, Sanders benched starting quarterback Julian Lewis and replaced him with Isaac Wilson. Lewis was a highly touted recruit out of high school last year but so far hasn't lived up to expectations at Colorado. Wilson, who transferred to Colorado this year after two years at Utah, is the brother of Saints quarterback Zach Wilson.

Lewis was 11-for-16 for 75 yards when he was benched. Wilson played slightly better, completing 12 of 25 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown.

Sanders has still never found a quarterback as good as his son, Shedeur, who started for Deion for two years at Jackson State and then two more years at Colorado. Overall, Deion's college coaching record is 36-14 with Shedeur as his quarterback and 9-15 without his son.

This year, Colorado is 2-2, and the schedule only gets tougher, with No. 11 Texas Tech and No. 15 Utah the next two opponents on the schedule. Sanders has an uphill battle ahead of him to get his team turned around.

item.title: Rules permit 12th player to hold ball on kickoffs without tee, regardless of weather
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: If teams want to use a 12th man to hold the ball for kickoffs, they can.
item.content:encoded:
If teams want to use a 12th man to hold the ball for kickoffs, they can. Without a tee, if they choose. Regardless of whether the wind requires it.

Although Bears special-teams coordinator Richard Hightower recently complained that the Eagles' use of a 12th man to hold the ball without a tee in order to better position it for a "dirty" kick violates the intent of the rules, the rules clearly allow it.

A league spokesperson has confirmed that teams are free to use a 12th man for that purpose. The kick can happen with or without a tee — and with or without a holder.

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni addressed the situation in a Saturday press conference.

"Obviously, with that, everything we're doing is within the rules of the game, and we'll continue to do the things that we need to do that give us the best chance to win each and every game," Sirianni said. "That's how we'll proceed as Philadelphia Eagles."

Hightower has said he hopes the rules change. Which implies that the rules, as written, do indeed allow teams to take advantage of the only circumstance in which it's permitted to have 12 players on the field.

Unless the rules are changed (and they rarely change during a given season), the message to all teams is clear. If you want to do it, you can. And if it makes it harder for the receiving team to field the ball, so be it.

item.title: Close-up images of field at Maracanã Stadium, a day before Ravens-Cowboys
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Ready or not, the Ravens and Cowboys will play on Sunday, at Maracanä Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
item.content:encoded:
Ready or not, the Ravens and Cowboys will play on Sunday, at Maracanä Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The field may not be ready. Not that it matters.

A close-up image of the playing surface has emerged, as posted by 105.3 The Fan. The synthetic grass that was stitched into the real grass is visible, even if not much real grass is visible.

As one source on the scene has put it, with a poetic flair, the field "looks like dog shit." (Hopefully, there wasn't a taste test.)

It doesn't matter. The game will be played. The league has said there is "no need to worry."

On Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, millions will see how it looks. More importantly for the NFL, it will be the third straight year with a game in Brazil. Which is important to the league's effort to attract more global fans.

Regardless of how the field looks, or how it plays.

item.title: Broncos put rookie RB Jonah Coleman on IR
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman scored his first NFL touchdown in Week 2, but he won't have a chance to add to that total for a while.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman scored his first NFL touchdown in Week 2, but he won't have a chance to add to that total for a while.

The Broncos placed Coleman on injured reserve Saturday. He had been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams on Friday and will now have to miss at least four games.

Coleman was pressed into duty with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey sidelined last weekend, but both backs are set to play on Sunday night.

The Broncos signed long snapper Mitchell Fraboni to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move. Fullback Adam Prentice and wide receiver Kolbe Katsis have been elevated from the practice squad and will revert back after facing the Rams.

item.title: Giants sign QB Jake Haener to 53-man roster
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants are planning to add a quarterback from outside the organization in the near future, but it won't happen before Sunday's game against the Titans.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants are planning to add a quarterback from outside the organization in the near future, but it won't happen before Sunday's game against the Titans.

Head coach John Harbaugh said on Friday that Jake Haener will be the backup to Jameis Winston in Week 3 and the team signed him off of the practice squad on Saturday. Haener signed with the Giants in August and returned to the practice squad after final cuts in August.

Haener made one start and appeared in eight games for the Saints in 2024. He was 18-of-39 for 226 yards, a touchdown and an interception.

The Giants also elevated wide receiver Braxton Berrios and linebacker Malik Harrison from the practice squad on a temporary basis.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Steelers' Saturday roster moves included the placement of one of their top rookies on injured reserve.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers' Saturday roster moves included the placement of one of their top rookies on injured reserve.

The team has announced that guard Jennings Dunker will be added to IR.

Dunker, a third-round pick from Iowa, was inactive for the first two games of the regular season.

He first appeared on the injury report on Thursday. Via Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Dunker suffered an MCL sprain during practice. He is expected to miss 4-6 weeks.

The Steelers filled Dunker's roster spot by signing running back Travis Homer from the practice squad. The Steelers also elevated running back Lew Nichols and defensive back Doneiko Slaughter from the practice squad.

The Steelers need the help at running back against the Bengals; Rico Dowdle is out with a toe injury, and Jaylen Warren is questionable with a shoulder injury.

item.description: The Chargers placed offensive lineman Trey Pipkins III on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers placed offensive lineman Trey Pipkins III on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.

Pipkins, who was ruled out for Week 3 with a knee injury, will miss at least the next four games.

With Kayode Awosika (fibula) also ruled out, Trevor Penning will start at left guard.

In a corresponding move, the team signed quarterback DJ Uiagalelei to the active roster. In addition, the Chargers elevated tight end Patrick Herbert and outside linebacker Caleb Murphy from the practice squad for Sunday’s game.

Backup quarterback Trey Lance popped up on Friday's injury report as questionable, prompting the Chargers to sign Uiagalelei to the active roster. He will backup Justin Herbert against the Bills if Lance is unavailable.

The Chargers are hurting at tight end with injuries to David Njoku and Charlie Kolar, so Patrick Herbert will add depth. Murphy is a core special teams player.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa is out for Sunday's game with a calf injury and he is expected to miss more time, so the team looked at a few options to bolster the position on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
49ers defensive end Nick Bosa is out for Sunday's game with a calf injury and he is expected to miss more time, so the team looked at a few options to bolster the position on Saturday.

The NFL's daily transactions report shows that Matt Judon, Julian Okwara, Jamin Davis, and Dawuane Smoot all tried out for the team.

Judon played 13 games for the Dolphins and one game for the Bills last season. He did not have any sacks after recording 72 of them over his first nine NFL seasons. Smoot had two sacks for the Jaguars last year, Davis appeared in two games for the Raiders, and Okwara was out of the league after being released by the Browns in August.

The 49ers also placed wide receiver Damarcus Robinson on injured reserve and signed defensive lineman Viliami Fehoko to the 53-man roster. Defensive linemen Kevin Givens and Sebastian Valdez were elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

item.title: Week 2 saw one fine for a hip-drop tackle, two fines for hits on defenseless players
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The NFL adopted a new policy regarding five player safety rules this offseason and the announcement of fines for Week 2 showed that there were three fouls in those categories.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL adopted a new policy regarding five player safety rules this offseason and the announcement of fines for Week 2 showed that there were three fouls in those categories.

Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was fined for a hip-drop tackle while Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton and Commanders defensive back Jeremy Reaves were fined for hits on defenseless players.

The new league policy calls for players to be suspended if they are guilty of three fouls of the same type in one season. The other fouls in the category are blindside blocks, launching and horse-collar tackles. Players can appeal the fines and they will receive half the fine amount back at the end of the season if they only commit one foul in a particular category.

There were also three qualifying fines in Week 1 and no player has picked up more than one fine through two weeks.

item.title: NFL fined 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk twice for imitating chugging a beer
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk took offense at a $14,926 fine he received this week for "engaging in offensive demonstrations."
item.content:encoded:
49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk took offense at a $14,926 fine he received this week for "engaging in offensive demonstrations." However, that was not his only fine this week.

Juszczyk was fined twice for his celebrations, each fine the same, for a total of $29,852.

One came on his 6-yard touchdown reception with 5:46 remaining in the third quarter, and the other came four plays earlier, following a 21-yard reception.

The NFL cited him for imitating chugging a beer in his celebrations, but Juszczyk said he was merely honoring his nickname of "Juice."

"I don't know how else to say it," Juszczyk said this week, via Nick Wagoner of ESPN. "I wasn’t drinking beer in my celebration. I think you guys all know my nickname is Juice. I have 'Juice' on my pads. The stadium yells 'Juice' when I catch the ball. When I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice, and it's been that way for years. I was as surprised as anybody when I got a fine."

Juszczyk is appealing after a previous appeal of a Week 1 fine of $20,033 for unnecessary roughness and leading with his helmet against the Rams.

The NFL also docked two other 49ers. Cornerback Upton Stout was fined $7,501 for taunting and defensive lineman Keion White drew a $13,770 fine for using his full body weight on a hit on Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis.

item.title: Tee Higgins, Amon-Ra St. Brown each fined four times for obscene gestures, illegal celebrations
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: We learned during the week that Bengals wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were fined for gestures deemed to be obscene by the league office, but it turns out that both players were fined multiple times.
item.content:encoded:
We learned during the week that Bengals wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were fined for gestures deemed to be obscene by the league office, but it turns out that both players were fined multiple times.

The NFL announced on Saturday that Higgins was fined three different times for making an obscene gesture. Higgins was also fined once for an illegal celebration/vulgar act during the win. All of the fines were for $14,926, which means Higgins's total bill was $59,704.

Chase received two fines for the same amount. They had company in Detroit when it came to being fined several times.

Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was fined four times for illegal celebrations or vulgar acts. He owes the league the same amount as Higgins for the infractions.

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, left tackle Penei Sewell and wide receiver Jameson Williams were also fined for the same infraction. Williams picked up a $11,941 fine for taunting as well.

There were 18 fines for obscene gestures or illegal celebrations/vulgar acts around the league in Week 2.

item.title: Roquan Smith fined for facemask on Tyler Shough on game-winning QB sneak
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Tyler Shough's fourth-down quarterback sneak for the game-winning touchdown was controversial.
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Shough's fourth-down quarterback sneak for the game-winning touchdown was controversial. The Saints quarterback may or may not have crossed the goal line, but replay upheld the on-field touchdown ruling with 1:28 left.

Officials, though, missed a facemask penalty against Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith on the play.

The NFL admitted the officiating error on Saturday by announcing an $11,941 fine for Smith for the facemask.

Ravens outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson was hit with a $17,911 fine for a hit on Shough before the 2-minute warning. He was penalized for putting his full body weight on Shough on the hit, helping the Saints get on the doorstep of the end zone.

Saints wide receiver Chris Olave will pay an $11,941 fine for taunting Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey. Officials penalized Olave during the game.
